title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, consolidate caches and bump GH Actions
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: our monolithic CI workflows are slow to iterate, have duplicated steps across lint/test/release flows, and produce cache key churn. This PR splits the monorepo CI into focused workflows (lint, unit/integration tests, release) and consolidates cache keys and shared actions. It also bumps GitHub Actions used by our workflows and upgrades Node.js matrices to Node 20 to align with the rest of the infra.

What this changes:
- Introduces three top-level workflows: .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml, ci-test.yml, ci-release.yml. Each workflow has a scoped matrix and explicit responsibility.
- Consolidates cache key strategy: repo-level restore keys + dependencies hash for package-lock/yarn.lock and toolchain-lock files to improve hit rate across jobs.
- Centralizes common steps into .github/actions/reusable/checkout-setup (small composite action) for consistent setup, restore-cache, and action versions.
- Bumps actions/setup-node -> v4, actions/checkout -> v4, cache/actions/cache -> v4 where safe.
- Updates node matrix to include node: [18, 20] with primary preference for 20.
- Improves job parallelism and sets default timeouts; reduces unnecessary job duplication for docs-only changes.

Testing and rollout:
- CI green on feature branch after 2 iterative runs (cache key fix and lint job timeout tweak).
- Canary: workflows scoped to run on PRs and push to main; release workflow gated behind labels and manual approval.
- Monitoring: added short-lived Slack alerts for workflow failures during the first week (ENG-4213).

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and verify triggers
- [x] Consolidate cache keys and validate hit rate improvements
- [x] Bump actions where compatibility tested
- [x] Update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md references to new CI commands
- [x] Reviewer approvals

Notes: there are intentionally small changes in a few repos to keep default behavior unchanged (release gating, branch protection). If this causes unexpected failures in downstream repos, revert the cache key change first (low risk).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Please confirm cache key format — I saw a cache miss on the second run (comment: adjusted restore keys to include repo name and lockfile hash).
Ava Chen (author): Adjusted cache restore keys and added fallback keys to improve hit rate. Re-ran CI and observed ~82% hit rate on test jobs.
Priya Kapoor: Can we reduce the default matrix to only node 20 for faster runs and keep node 18 as optional? I worry about CI minutes.
Ava Chen (author): Switched matrix ordering so node 20 runs first and node 18 is run only for 'compatibility' label; preserved node 18 for a short window. This keeps default PR turnaround faster.
Liam O'Connor: Approved — small nits about step names and a comment on timeout values. Verified release gating is manual and labels work as expected.
CI Bot: Build passed on run #3 (cache restored). All required checks are green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge on 2026-03-02 after approvals. Final commit message: 'refactor(ci): split workflows and consolidate caches — squash merge'.
release_notes: Refactor CI: split lint/test/release workflows, consolidate cache key strategy, bump GitHub Actions and primary Node.js to 20. Improves PR iteration time and cache hit rates. No user-facing changes.
notes_for_revert: If regressions appear (failed restores or degraded cache hit rate), revert the cache-key changes in scripts/ci/cache-keys.sh first and re-run CI. Release workflow is gated and safe to roll back separately.
